evidence: The claim depends on process.env persisting across test files in a worker. The agent cited jest-util createProcessEnv, which copies env for each file, and reported a --runInBand probe that saw exactly one --import= entry per file. The round 2 reviewer withdrew the point on the same per-file isolation argument.
This duplicates F1. The reviewer misread the adjacent socket comment, which is about the shared pid, not a shared env object. Jest gives each file its own env copy, so the append cannot accumulate.

The Rust NODE_FLAGS list mirrored a TS fact that check-protocol.mjs did not check, unlike every other mirrored vocabulary. The fix added a TS NODE_FLAGS const plus a memberSet row, and the agent negative-checked it by dropping -V.
guidance_note: When adding a Rust-side mirror of a TS fact, add the check-protocol.mjs row in the same commit, as every existing mirrored vocabulary already has.

evidence: The throw message said 'run under jest (globals)', but jest.config.js had no globals key. The agent acknowledged that the PR had replaced that mechanism and reworded the message to name scripts/version-stamp.cjs.
guidance_note: When a PR swaps one mechanism for another mid-development, grep the new file's comments and error strings for the old mechanism's name before pushing.

evidence: The agent confirmed that the harness's --daemon tsx path spawns raw source without the stamp. It took the reviewer's first remedy (preload the stamp) and rejected the 'dev' fallback, which the ticket was deleting. However, the fix set NODE_OPTIONS by plain assignment, which dropped the operator's own value and produced F10/F11.
guidance_note: Before making a module-load throw mandatory, grep every entry point that runs raw source (scripts/, harnesses) and give each the stamp. When injecting NODE_OPTIONS, merge with the existing value instead of assigning.

evidence: No test exercised the TS --version/-V branch, while the Rust side pinned the contract. The agent added a spawn test that asserts stdout and the exit code, which tests behavior rather than the argv predicate.
guidance_note: When one side of a cross-language contract gains a routing test, add the matching test on the answering side in the same PR.

evidence: This is the same breakage as F5, seen from stats.ts: the daemon now imports PACKAGE_VERSION at load. The same harness-preload fix resolves it. Rejecting the fallback was correct.
guidance_note: Before adding a throwing import to a module the daemon loads at startup, list every path that runs the daemon from source.

evidence: The header comment cited Jest's 'globals (jest.config.js)', which did not exist. It now names scripts/version-stamp.cjs.
guidance_note: Sweep the header comments of a new file for a mechanism the PR itself abandoned mid-development.

evidence: This is the third copy of the F1 claim, here labelled a 'resource leak'. Jest's per-file env copy makes the accumulation impossible. The agent supported the pushback with an empirical probe.

The F5/F7 fix (731fc17) added `NODE_OPTIONS: --import=...` after `...process.env`, which replaced an operator's NODE_OPTIONS that had previously passed through. The agent made withStamp() one merge used by both callers instead of a second hand-written append.
guidance_note: When a fix copies a pattern from a sibling call site (test/setup.ts already appended), reuse or extract that code instead of rewriting it, so the merge semantics come along.

evidence: This duplicates F10: in 731fc17 the harness env assigned NODE_OPTIONS and dropped preset flags such as --max-old-space-size. The withStamp helper fixed it, and the agent verified with a preset NODE_OPTIONS.
guidance_note: When writing an env var that operators commonly set (NODE_OPTIONS, PATH), merge with the existing value by default.

evidence: The reviewer flagged its own concern as unverified. The agent pointed out that jest runs without --experimental-vm-modules, so ts-jest emits CJS and __filename exists. test/version.test.ts imports src/version in-process and passes, so the stamp reaches the realm that version.ts reads. The createRequire line predates the round-1 fix, so this is not fix-caused.

The flagged commit be11d33 touched only the harness, version-stamp.cjs and setup.ts, so the post-review flag on help-text.ts is incidental. The F3 fix, however, created a single NODE_FLAGS const and left help-text.ts's '-V, --version' line hand-typed, another consumer of the same vocabulary. The agent moved NODE_FLAGS to cli-flags.ts and rendered both help lines from it.
guidance_note: When creating a single source for a vocabulary, grep for every literal spelling of its members (help text, docs, tests) and make each one derive from it in the same commit.

evidence: The `version` field really does change type from number to string under the same key. The agent says there are no external consumers and that the semantic-release changelog records the split from the squash commit, which answers the 'note it somewhere' ask. The law was cited against a compat alias the reviewer never proposed. The StatsSnapshot change was in the original diff, so the be11d33 flag is incidental.

narrative: Round 0 raised three duplicate env-growth findings, which the agent correctly refuted with Jest internals and a probe. It also caught a real harness breakage from the new throwing version module. The harness fix assigned NODE_OPTIONS instead of merging it, which cost round 1 (F10/F11) and was resolved with a shared withStamp helper. Round 2 raised an unverified realm concern, refuted by passing in-process tests. Round 3 found that the F3 single-source NODE_FLAGS left help-text hand-typed.
guidance_observations: When a fix reproduces logic that already exists at a sibling call site, extracting it on the first pass would have saved a full round here.
Each single-source-of-truth fix should be followed by a grep for literal spellings of the moved facts; the help-text line was missed and cost a round.
The empirical pushbacks (Jest env probe, in-process import test) were well supported and short.

evidence: The new test calls `new Response(...)`. The eslint block covers **/*.ts, but only fetch and AbortSignal had been added as globals. Response was added in 3045eab.
guidance_note: When adding runtime globals to the eslint list, include every global the new tests use, not only those in src/.

evidence: The reply-hint says pushback, but the reply opens 'Plan: valid'. parseReleaseVersion(PACKAGE_VERSION) threw before staging, which contradicted 'the verdict informs, it never fails the install'. The fix makes the parse a typed failure folded into `unchecked` and removes the precondition.
guidance_note: When a feature is described as advisory, check every throw on its path before the PR; the stamp-side parse threw while the registry-side parse was already folded into `unchecked`.

evidence: The network call is real, but AbortSignal.timeout caps it at 5s and every failure degrades to `unchecked` with exit 0, once per install. Refusing an ownerless flag is defensible. Part of the pushback was false: 'adds no wall-clock at all' was disproved by F7's spawnSync finding.
This is the same throw as F2, framed as stamp/registry asymmetry. The shared fix added a test that '1.42.0-beta.1' with a good lookup yields `unchecked` naming the stamp.
guidance_note: Handle both sides of a comparison the same way: if a malformed registry value folds into a verdict, the malformed local value should too.

evidence: The never-fails contract is enforced in the currency seam, not in runInstall. After the F2 fix, assessCurrency is total, and a composed test pins 'non-release stamp + unreachable registry → still a report'. The banner ordering was verified live with `node dist/index.mjs install`. Mocking osacompile and lsregister to test ordering would test structure.

The agent checked that both encoded forms return 200 on registry.npmjs.org. It did not say the unencoded form failed, so 'every request 404s' was speculative. Encoding matches npm's client and costs nothing, so accepting was reasonable.
guidance_note: When building a registry URL from a scoped package name, encode the name segment the way the npm client does.

evidence: The ON-NAMED-FIX-COMMIT flag is a false positive here. 3045eab did not touch the early `const latest = fetchLatestVersion(...)` or its concurrency comment, both present in the round-0 hunk. The premise holds: spawnSync blocks the loop while the wall-clock timeout runs. The agent moved the fetch to after the synchronous work.
guidance_note: Before claiming that an async operation runs concurrently with later work, check whether that work uses spawnSync or other sync calls that block the event loop.

narrative: Round 0 found a real asymmetry: a malformed local stamp threw and aborted the install, while a malformed registry value degraded gracefully. Two duplicate threads covered it, and the fix made the parse a typed failure folded into `unchecked`. The opt-out flag and integration-test asks were reasonably declined or redirected to the seam. Round 1's spawnSync finding concerned original code, not the fix, and was fixed by moving the fetch.
guidance_observations: The agent's F3 pushback stated a concurrency claim ('adds no wall-clock') without checking for sync calls in the staging path; the reviewer disproved it a round later.
Fixes were complete on the first pass: no finding traces to a fix commit.

evidence: makeDiagnosticLink truncates to 8 lines, and the build warning was appended after per-config warnings. The reviewer's own option ('put it first') was taken as a one-token reorder. The agent noted the general '…more' indicator is already tracked as candybar-diagnostics-avi.
guidance_note: When joining a new message onto a capped channel, put the higher-priority message first.

evidence: The agent noted that the tsx harness always yields `not-source-checkout`, so the join had only ever run with null. It added an e2e test that spawns the built bundle from a scratch checkout and asserts the row ordering.
guidance_note: When the test harness runs from source but the feature only activates in the built layout, add an e2e test against the built bundle before review.

evidence: The agent found a real src/.DS_Store in the checkout. It chose a deny-list for dotfiles and ~ backups over an extension allow-list that would duplicate tsdown's import graph, and added tests.
guidance_note: For an mtime walk, list which non-source files appear in a source tree (Finder, editor swap and backup files) before writing the walk.

evidence: The walk really is synchronous on the event loop, but the agent measured 0.60 ms over 126 files once a minute, comparable to the sibling armBinaryWatch statSync. Going async would add overlap state to save under a millisecond.

Dirent.isDirectory() is false for symlinks, so the comment 'directories recurse' contradicted the code; the walk code dates from round 0, so this is not fix-caused. Following links as the reviewer suggested produced cycles (F7/F8) and external-tree walks (F11). In F11 the agent called this 'the trade the earlier round's fix got backwards' and switched to lstat, treating links as entries.
guidance_note: When a reviewer proposes following symlinks in a recursive walk, decide first whether a link is an entry or a path, and list the cycle and external-tree consequences before accepting.

evidence: The original walk's statSync threw on a dangling link every sample, which parked the verdict at `unchecked`. The agent used throwIfNoEntry:false for absence but kept EACCES loud rather than skipping every failure. That is a narrower fix than the reviewer's 'skip any bad entry'.
guidance_note: When writing a filesystem walk, separate 'entry vanished' from 'entry unreadable' from the start.

evidence: Cycles became possible only once the F5 fix (78ac0c3) made recursion follow stat through symlinks. The agent added a realpath visited set, which F11's fix then deleted in favour of lstat. Cycle safety is not temporal coupling, so the law does not fit.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a walk follow links, check for cycles and out-of-tree targets in the same commit.

evidence: This duplicates F7 on the same line. The unbounded recursion through `ln -s . src/loop` exists only because of the F5 link-following fix. The visited-set cure was replaced one round later.
guidance_note: When a fix makes a walk follow links, check for cycles and out-of-tree targets in the same commit.

evidence: The F6 fix split vanished from unreadable but tested only the dangling case. The reviewer's chmod-0 file test would not have thrown, as the agent noted, since stat needs only directory permission. The agent tested a chmod-000 directory, which yields `unchecked` naming EACCES.
guidance_note: When a fix introduces a two-way split in error handling, add a test for each branch in that commit.

evidence: For a persistently unreadable directory the pushback is right: skipping the subtree would report `current` over source the walk never saw. The reply's claim that the vanish race is 'already a non-event via throwIfNoEntry' is false for a directory removed between the parent's stat and its readdirSync/realpathSync. That gap is outside the F6 sweep, though it self-heals on the next sample.
guidance_note: When making a vanish race harmless for files, apply the same treatment to the directory-level reads (readdir, realpath) in the same walk.

evidence: Walking a large external tree through a symlink became possible only with the F5 link-following fix. The agent rejected depth caps and switched to lstatSync, deleting the visited set and realpath, which makes cycles and external walks impossible to represent.
guidance_note: When a reviewer proposes following symlinks in a recursive walk, decide first whether a link is an entry or a path, and list the cycle and external-tree consequences before accepting.

narrative: Round 0 fixes were solid: reorder, e2e test, dotfile filter, and a measured perf pushback. In round 1 the agent accepted the reviewer's cure for symlinked directories (follow links), which opened cycles (round 2) and external-tree walks (round 3). In round 3 the agent reversed the decision with lstat, treating links as entries. The F6 vanished/unreadable split also left an untested EACCES branch and an uncovered directory-level race, raised in round 3.
guidance_observations: Accepting a reviewer's 'follow the symlink' cure without working out what that changes about the walk cost two rounds; the agent later called it backwards.
Each round's edge-case fix to the walk invited the next edge; deciding the walk's semantics first (lstat, links as entries) ended the series in one change.
Measured pushbacks (0.60 ms walk) were well supported and stood.
